standard_prerequisites.name: Primitive recursion schema
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function defined from primitive recursive g and h by f(0)=g, f(n+1)=h(n,f(n)) is primitive recursive.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the schema the displayed equations instantiate (738-747).

standard_prerequisites.name: Concatenation of Goedel numbers
standard_prerequisites.statement: The concatenation operation on coded symbol sequences is primitive recursive, established earlier in the unit, and Goedel numbers of individual symbols are constants.
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes the recursion step a primitive recursive term in n and num(n) (738-747).

core_obligations: Base: num(0) = the Goedel number of the symbol 0, a constant (739-741).
Step: num(n+1) = the Goedel number of the prime symbol concatenated with num(n) concatenated with the Goedel number of the closing parenthesis (742-745).
Both the base and the step are built from constants and the primitive-recursive concatenation, so num is primitive recursive by the schema (738-747).

proof_roadmap.step: Read off the primitive recursion defining num.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 733-736: the function num(n) giving the Goedel number of the numeral for n is primitive recursive. The author proof (738-747) is complete as an explicit primitive recursion: num(0) is the Goedel number of the symbol 0, and num(n+1) concatenates the Goedel numbers of the prime symbol, num(n), and the closing parenthesis. The recursion schema with the constant and concatenation functions already established primitive recursive in the unit yields the claim; nothing beyond the unit's established stock is used.
